brief_extract: While this fact may seem unimportant to many of our readers, there is no doubt at all that it is anything but insignificant in the eyes of the government, the Equal Opportunities Commission and the computer industry itself. brief_context: Comparing the EAW Director role to other organisations in Britain.
article_title: Inside Headquarters: Mrs ANN McMULLAN talks of her work as Director and Secretary of the EAW
brief_extract:
At the same time, the NEC delegates to her authority for the day-to-day management of the Association and responsibility for resolving problems as they arise. A Unique Post
The post of Director EAW has always been unique amongst women's organisations in Britain carrying, as it does, not only the responsibilities of a General Secretaryship, but also a considerable proportion of the responsibilities borne in other women's organisations by the chairman or her deputies. This is necessitated by the technical nature of the EAW's working commitments, which call for continuous day-to-day attention, and a depth of knowledge which can be acquired only through long-term, full-time involvement.

brief_context: Location of extensive work travel for Mrs McMullan.
article_title: Inside Headquarters: Mrs ANN McMULLAN talks of her work as Director and Secretary of the EAW
brief_extract: A high degree of self-motivation is called for, as well as the ability to grasp at an early stage the significance of situations as they arise on a national or local basis in order to promote effectively the many activities of the EAW. Mrs McMullan represents the EAW on numerous committees including: Advisory Committee on Safety of Domestic Electrical Equipment; British Electro-Technical Approvals Board (BEAB), General Council; British Approvals Board for Telecommunications (BABT); National Inspection Council for Electrical Installation Contracting (NICEIC); Women's Council; UK Federation for Education in Home Economics; St John Ambulance, Director General's Association Committee, and also Public Affairs Committee. As chairman of the EAW PR Syndicate, which she originated in 1980, Mrs McMullan personally fulfills the roles of PR manager, chief press officer and chief information officer of the Association.

brief_extract:
A Wartime Start
Mrs McMullan started her career as an Operations Plotter in the WAAF at Fighter Command Headquarters, later becoming a Code and Cypher Officer with additional administrative responsibilities. Marriage took her to Germany where her husband was stationed, and later to South Africa. It was in Germany, as a member of a British relief committee visiting camps for displaced persons that, as she said, "I became aware of the great importance of home making, even in the most depressing conditions."
Welfare work followed with the WVS and in South Africa where she was Organising Secretary for a scheme for feeding African children.
